answer: Like a quill signing each work order in a distinct pigment, an agent must attach a verifiable proof-of-work receipt to every transaction: a small, unique computation whose delta cost grows with the number of identities it claims. A single identity is cheap, but a Sybil farm spawning ten thousand fake agents must pay ten thousand times the compute and electricity, while honest agents pay once. Reputation then attaches to the costly identity, so creating a fresh fake to escape a bad record costs more than behaving honestly.
